name: WS2812B 16x16 LED matrix (256 pixels)
description: Flexible 16×16 matrix of 256 individually addressable WS2812B RGB LEDs (Worldsemi, 24-bit GRB, 800 kbit/s single-wire data) chained in a zig-zag on a 160×160 mm FPC with 10 mm pitch. Runs on 5 V (datasheet absolute range 3.5–5.3 V); about 60 mA per LED at full white (0.3 W), so up to about 15.4 A (77 W) for the whole panel: it always needs its own 5 V supply. Sold as: BTF-LIGHTING WS2812B 16x16 256-pixel flexible LED panel (160×160 mm black FPC, 3-pin JST-SM input 5V, DIN, GND; matching 5V, DOUT, GND output for chaining; extra red/white power-injection wires).
eli5: A soft square of 256 colour lights you can set one by one, like a small screen, using just one data wire, but it needs its own big power supply.

pins.name: 5V
pins.description: LED supply, 5 V (3.5–5.3 V absolute maximum). Up to about 15.4 A for 256 LEDs at full white: feed it from a separate 5 V supply (10–20 A) whose GND joins the board's GND, never from the board's 5V/VBUS pin.

pins.name: DIN
pins.description: Data in to the first LED (input JST-SM; follow the arrows). Needs at least 0.7 × VDD (3.5 V at 5 V) as a high: 3.3 V GPIO is marginal, so use a 74AHCT125 level shifter and a 300–500 Ω series resistor.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground, shared with the microcontroller and the 5 V supply

buildNotes: Wire the 3-pin JST-SM INPUT connector (5V, DIN, GND printed by the pads); the output connector (5V, DOUT, GND) only chains to another panel.

Power the panel from a separate regulated 5 V supply (5 V 10 A for typical animations, 20 A for full white at full brightness) and join its GND to the board's GND. Use the extra red/white power wires to inject power too, with 18 AWG or thicker leads; without injection the far LEDs look dim or yellow.
The driver's default brightness of 0.1 keeps a full-white frame near 1.5 A (256 × 6 mA), still more than a USB-powered board can give. Even dark, the 256 LEDs draw roughly 0.2–0.3 A.
Put a 1000 µF capacitor across 5V and GND at the panel and a 300–500 Ω resistor in series with DIN.
WS2812B wants a data high of at least 0.7 × VDD (3.5 V at 5 V): 3.3 V data is marginal; use a 74AHCT125 level shifter powered from 5 V for reliable data.
Never exceed 5.3 V on the panel's supply (datasheet absolute maximum).

driver.code:
# WS2812B 16x16 flexible LED matrix (256 pixels), MicroPython helper.
# Uses MicroPython's built-in neopixel module, which produces the WS2812B's
# 800 kbit/s single-wire code (T0H 0.4 us, T1H 0.8 us, +-150 ns) and sends each
# pixel as 24 bits in G-R-B order, MSB first, as the Worldsemi datasheet requires.
# A low gap of more than 50 us after write() latches the new colours.
#
# The flexible 16x16 panels are wired in a zig-zag (serpentine): row 0 runs away
# from the DIN corner, row 1 runs back, and so on. If your panel is wired
# row-by-row in one direction, pass serpentine=False.
#
# brightness scales every colour (0.0-1.0). Each LED draws about 60 mA at full
# white, so the whole panel can pull about 15 A at 5 V. The default of 0.1 keeps a
# full-white frame near 1.5 A: still too much for a board's USB 5 V pin, so always
# feed the panel from a separate 5 V supply whose GND joins the board's GND.
import neopixel

WIDTH = 16
HEIGHT = 16


class Matrix16x16:
    WIDTH = WIDTH
    HEIGHT = HEIGHT

    def __init__(self, pin, serpentine=True, brightness=0.1):
        self.np = neopixel.NeoPixel(pin, WIDTH * HEIGHT)
        self.serpentine = serpentine
        self.brightness = max(0.0, min(1.0, brightness))

    def index(self, x, y):
        """Chain position of the pixel at column x, row y (0,0 = first LED after DIN)."""
        if not (0 <= x < WIDTH and 0 <= y < HEIGHT):
            raise ValueError('x and y must be 0-15')
        if self.serpentine and y & 1:
            x = WIDTH - 1 - x
        return y * WIDTH + x

    def _scale(self, color):
        b = self.brightness
        return (int(color[0] * b), int(color[1] * b), int(color[2] * b))

    def pixel(self, x, y, color):
        """Set one pixel to color = (r, g, b), 0-255 each. Call show() to send."""
        self.np[self.index(x, y)] = self._scale(color)

    def get(self, x, y):
        """The (r, g, b) bytes that will be sent for the pixel at x, y (after brightness)."""
        return self.np[self.index(x, y)]

    def fill(self, color):
        self.np.fill(self._scale(color))

    def clear(self):
        self.np.fill((0, 0, 0))

    def show(self):
        self.np.write()

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time
from ws2812b_16x16 import Matrix16x16

m = Matrix16x16(Pin({DIN}), brightness=0.1)
m.clear()
m.show()
time.sleep(1)
for y in range(16):
    for x in range(16):
        m.pixel(x, y, (250, 0, 0) if x == y else (0, 0, 120))
m.show()
print('diag', m.get(5, 5), 'bg', m.get(1, 0), 'index', m.index(0, 1))
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
